sources.entry: Healthchecks - Listen for pings and sends alerts when pings are late. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Python/Docker
Healthchecks | Cron job and background task monitoring with alerts

summary.one_liner: Healthchecks is a self-hostable cron job and background task monitoring service that listens for HTTP or email pings and sends alerts when pings arrive late.
summary.what_it_does: Checks are defined by a Period and Grace Time, or by a cron expression (parsed with the cronsim library). Jobs signal they ran by sending an HTTP request or an email to a unique address, and Healthchecks sends alerts when a ping is missing past its grace time. It provides a web dashboard with live status, a per-check event log, public hard-to-guess status badges, and an API. It supports 25+ notification integrations (for example Slack, Discord, Pushover, Signal, Telegram, Matrix, PagerDuty, Apprise) and monthly email reports. Management commands handle alert sending (sendalerts), reports (sendreports), an SMTP listener for email pings (smtpd), and cleanup of old pings and accounts. Optional features include WebAuthn 2FA, external authentication via proxy headers, team projects with read-only access, and S3-compatible object storage for large ping bodies.
use_cases: monitor cron jobs and scheduled tasks
get alerted when a backup script stops running
send job failure alerts to Slack, Discord, or Telegram
show public status badges for scheduled jobs
self-host a dead man's switch monitoring service
how_to_run: A Dockerfile and prebuilt Docker images are available; the Docker images run migrations and sendalerts/sendreports/smtpd automatically.
stack: PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB (SQLite by default in development)
notable: Email pings: a built-in SMTP listener lets cron jobs ping by sending an email to a check's unique address
Cron-expression schedules as an alternative to fixed period and grace time
WebAuthn two-factor authentication and external authentication via trusted proxy headers
Shell Commands integration runs local commands on up/down events
Optional S3-compatible storage for large ping bodies
caveats: Production use requires a reverse proxy for TLS, a process manager for sendalerts and sendreports, and a configured SMTP server for email
Docker images do not handle TLS termination
Shell Commands integration is a security risk unless all users are fully trusted; it is disabled by default
Deleted checks' stored objects in external storage must be cleaned up manually with pruneobjects; there is no script to migrate ping bodies back from object storage to the database
